paragraphs: This building was built in 2015 and was named for Carl F. Jacobs (who started the NMSU music department) and Marion Hardmen (retired English Professor and Dean of Women).

Hardman and Jacobs Undergraduate Learning Center houses classrooms of various sizes that are centrally scheduled and used for many of the university's core curriculum classes and larger classes. Most undergraduates will take at least some courses in the undergraduate learning center during their student careers. The center also houses the Student Success Center, which includes TRiO Student Support Services and TRiO Upward Bound, and Information & Communications Technology, which includes a Help Desk, computer labs, a drop-in computer center, computer rentals and computer offices and workshops.

This building is a LEED Gold certified building. LEED, or Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design, is a program that strives to create a more sustainable world. This building has been specifically designed to use fewer resources and decrease waste. You can find more information about this program here.

paragraphs: The bidding for the construction of the Chemistry Building, Gardiner Hell, and Jett Hall all opened the same day in 1955. Jett Hall occupies the southern side of the Horseshoe. This building was constructed with Jett Annex in 1957, and in 1965 the northeast, east, and West wings were added along with improvements to the entrance. After more than 60 years, Jett Hall is still home to the chemical, mechanical, and aerospace engineering departments. The hall was named after Daniel Boone Jett, a beloved former dean of the College of Engineering and a professor of civil engineering for 30 years.

This building was constructed in 1968 and named after Roger B. Corbett, the President of NMSU from 1955-1970. The original plan for the building was much different from what you see today. The original location for the building was to be approximately where Educational Services building is today behind Garcia Hall. Also the original plan was only two stories but featured a planetarium, bowling lanes, billiard and table tennis, a bookstore, administrative offices, and room for games, hobbies, a dark room, etc.

Corbett Center, the university's student union, is a bustling center of activity on campus. It is home to the several dining establishments and many student organizations and programs. Corbett Center also offers attractive conference facilities.

Science Hall was built in 1987. There is a dedication plaque on this building from the Board of Regents. The Science Hall is home to the departments of Computer Science, Mathematical Sciences, Women's Studies, Sociology, and Psychology. Science Hall contains 119,295 square feet of laboratories, classroom space, and faculty offices.

Foster Hall is home of the Department of Biology. The original building, constructed in 1930, is on the National Register of Historic Places and is named after former NMSU President Luther Foster. Six years after construction, a fresco was added by Santa Fe artist Olive Rush as part of the Public Arts Project. The fresco was restored in 1983. A recent renovation added 17,000 square feet of space for faculty offices, laboratories and classrooms to that expansion.

The Astronomy Building was built in 1959 and is home to the Department of Astronomy. This department owns several telescopes, which they've distributed amongst the observatories throughout campus. NASA also uses this building as a Planetary Node, which collects atmospheric data. The node also provides academic research materials for both staff and students.
Hadley Hall is home to several administrative units including the President's Office and Human Resources. It was built in 1953 and named after Hiram Hadley, the university's first President.

Breland Hall, originally designed to be a men's dormitory, is home to many departments in the School Arts and Sciences. The idea to create the building began in 1954 and construction was finished on September 1, 1956. The hall was named for the late Rufus Galloway Breland, Professor of English, 1925-28, and Head of the English Department from 1928 until the time of his death on December 27, 1940. In 1976, Breland Hall was remodeled at a cost of $1.9 million to accommodate the College of Arts and Sciences, offices, classrooms, Arts and Sciences Departments, and laboratories. In addition, Breland Hall also houses the college's academic advisors.

This building, home to the Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry, was built in 1957 and was remodeled and expanded in 1996. Home to laboratories, classrooms, research instrumentation and faculty offices, the Chemistry Building is located along the north leg of the "horseshoe" and is one of several buildings containing facilities utilized by the Department of Chemistry. Chemistry graduate students may use facilities at nearby White Sands Missile Range, including a linear accelerator, a deuterium-tritium generator, a fast-burst reactor, counting equipment, and extensive computer equipment.

In 1959, a new women's physical education gymnasium was built. It was named Rentfrow Gym after Era Rentfrow, a woman who spent most of her life at NMSU. She enrolled in preparatory school in 1911, graduated in 1919, and was the university registrar from 1922 to 1959. This gymnasium is currently home to the College of Education's Department of Kinesiology and Dance.

Gerald Thomas is home to the College of Agriculture, Consumer, and Environmental Sciences. It was built in 1963. Gerald Thomas Hall was designed by Wolgamood and Millington Architects. The hall was named for Gerald Thomas, former NMSU President from 1970 through 1984. In addition to classrooms, laboratories and faculty offices, Gerald Thomas is also home to the Chile Pepper Institute, which can be found in room 265.

paragraphs: Gardiner Hall is home to the Department of Physics and contains faculty offices, classrooms, and laboratory space. It was built in 1957 and named after George Gardiner, a physics professor and founder of the Physical Science Laboratory.

This building is a LEED Silver certified building. LEED, or Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design, is a program that strives to create a more sustainable world. This building has been specifically designed to use fewer resources and decrease waste. You can find more information about this program here.
